newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs shed gains, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs shed gains, seen consolidating.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures took a breather for the first time on Wednesday after Japan's general election results sent them hurtling towards daily new contract highs.

Dealers said both ends of the Japanese yield curve were sold off in afternoon trade following reports of comments by Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita, which seemed to diverge from his traditional position on the economy.

Matsushita was reported to have said that the mechanism for an autonomous Japanese economic recovery was now in place but the market later took heart from reports quoting the BOJ chief saying the recovery was not yet sustainable.
This kept the lead June Euroyen contract from falling below a low of 99.23 in late trade, after it hit a new high of 99.40 against its IMM close at 99.24.
"The market's been very overbought since the elections. It just got too euphoric and when people wanted to get out, there was a narrow door," said a trader with a European institution.
He said June Euroyen could lose another five ticks before it stabilised.
"The market will wait for the next tankan or something concrete before going higher," said a dealer with a Japanese futures house.
"In the near term, if June Euroyen goes anywhere above 99.30, I would short the market," he added.
But he said the BOJ was likely to hold rates steady until the middle of next year as the Japanese economy looked like it was making "a very slow, painful recovery."
December JGBs settled at 123.88 against their opening 123.98 after reaching a contract high of 124.40 in early trade.
Eurodollar futures pared early losses to end steady after an overnight decline on U.S. treasury markets where sentiment was hurt by supply concerns following a two-year note auction.
March Eurodollars finished unchanged against their IMM close at 94.29 on low volume of 3,300 lots.
